title: Dynamic entitlement lattice and autoscale safeguard language
creator: Maya Chen
description: Draft contract annex and SLO specification that defines: 1) a multi-dimensional throughput entitlement model (the 'entitlement lattice') which allocates guaranteed tokens/sec across request classes and zones; 2) an error-budget accounting method tied to throughput shortfalls and latency regressions; 3) deterministic credit calculation and automatic credit issuance; and 4) the autoscale interlock and fleet control rules that govern when we will attempt capacity remediation (reserved pool expansion, preemptible fallback, cross-AZ routing) versus when credits are applied. This ticket covers language, measurement definition, and the operational playbook to hand to Legal and Professional Services.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable contract annex draft describing the entitlement lattice and the crediting algorithm exists and is reviewed by Legal
SLO definitions (metrics, windows, quantiles) for each request class are specified with query examples for internal metrics (PromQL) and external reporting CSV format
Error-budget burn rules that map to credit amounts (USD or token-equivalent) are computed with worked examples for 3 outage scenarios
Autoscale interlock: documented trigger thresholds, ramp windows, and pre/post actions (AZ reroute, reserve pool grow, throttle policy) with failure-mode decision tree
Operational runbook with notification templates and customer notice timing (Initial, 2-hour update, remediation notice, credit invoice) is included
Legal and Solutions Engineering have signed off on the remediation playbook and credit formula

2026-03-04 Arjun Patel: Eng proposal linked; prefer 1-minute granularity for tokens/sec SLA measurement to reduce noise, but will aggregate to 5-min windows for contract enforcement.

decisions: Measure SLA on a per-request-class basis: interactive (P95 latency + tokens/sec), streaming (sustained tokens/sec), batch (throughput windows)
Error budget tied to per-class throughput shortfall relative to entitlement lattice; latency regressions consume budget proportionally based on request-class SLO weight
Automatic credits applied as percentage-of-monthly-dedicated-fee, computed from token-equivalent shortfall to avoid per-token accounting complexity
Autoscale interlock will attempt non-invasive mitigations first (reserve pool, AZ reroute) before issuing credits; sequence and timing documented in runbook
Customers will receive a notification flow (initial, hourly updates, remediation complete + credit line item) with templated language and SLA breach explanation
open_questions: How should we attribute cross-tenant capacity contention localized in a single AZ? (customer gets credit vs account for platform-level degradation)
Should we provide customers the right to request manual failover to a different model variant that may change cost characteristics?
What is the maximum automatic reserve pool growth allowed per customer before violating other customers' entitlements?
Edge-case: how to treat scheduled maintenance windows that overlap multiple customers in the same host pool?
notes_for_legal: Draft language proposes credits as percentage of monthly committed fee (worked examples attached). Legal to confirm enforceability across multi-region hosting and confirm notification windows. Include explicit carve-outs for provider-wide incidents.
